# Gothic automatic line metrics

These are original controls generated by `tools/mixed_symbol_line_fixture.py`
with python-docx (MIT) and lxml (BSD). No corpus XML, standalone font files, or external
renderer is included. The reference application opened the exact
source read-only and exported `controls-native.pdf`. The reference extractor
records source/PDF hashes and every native text origin and baseline.

The 58 pages cover:

- Mixed Calibri/MS Gothic lines, ordinary X versus checkbox, at 9pt and 11pt,
  both in paragraphs and table cells, with surrounding blank/body paragraphs.
- Pure Calibri, MS Gothic, MS PGothic and MS UI Gothic at 6, 9, 11, 20, 48, 96
  and 144pt, using short samples to avoid wrapping at the large sizes.
- Synthetic bold, italic and bold italic in the three Gothic faces at 9/20pt.

The Gothic collection's installed font tables have 256 units per em, ascent
220, descent 36 and zero line gap. CSS normal line height reports the same
one-em geometry. The reference application uses a larger automatic line box: at 9pt its consecutive
baseline advances are 11.64/11.76pt; at 96pt, 124.47/124.58pt; at 144pt,
186.74/186.87pt. Its PDF coordinates have small output rounding differences.
The combined baseline/advance measurements fit 38 additional design units on
each side of the line. Mixed lines independently test how that box combines
with Calibri's extents. The character itself and table membership do not cause
the discrepancy.

`face-metrics.js` applies this compatibility profile only to the three
verified family names when their measured base ascent/descent also match.
Substituted faces and all other families retain their measured metrics. This
is not a general rule for East Asian fonts, nor an adjustment to glyph outlines,
point sizes, or DOCX formatting. The profile is resolved with the existing
per-face metrics cache, without new font reads or per-character measurement.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) and §17.18.48 (`ST_LineSpacingRule`)
define automatic line spacing. The additional native leading is reference
compatibility evidence, not a formula prescribed by those clauses. The raw
reference and explicit scope are retained rather than claiming a general
OpenType metric selection algorithm.

The browser regression compares every nonblank line and origin with the reference application,
checks the local faces are available, and exercises exact no-edit/undo package
preservation, a body edit and export/reopen. Unit guards cover other families,
changed/substituted geometry and immutable input metrics.

All 232 measured baselines match within 0.183pt. The reference is not a claim
of pixel-identical glyph antialiasing between the native reference PDF renderer and Canvas.
